title: APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms
exclusions: Out of scope for non-APC chilled-water CRAC strings without traps or polls in the APC enterprise MIB tree, environments where SNMP from NMC to Splunk is disabled and no alternate poller exists, and pure predictive thermal analytics that do not ingest these SNMP feeds. Does not certify compliance with any specific regulation.
evidence: Scheduled saved search or alert "UC_15_1_31_APICoolingFault" against `index=power` with CSV export disabled but email/pdf digest to facilities; paired Dashboard Studio timeline and table panels filtered to `sourcetype=snmp:trap` or `snmp:apc:cooling`, retained per your internal evidence policy.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-15.1.31 positive (APC, InRow, and, Airflow, Unit): ingest synthetic events into `index=power` sourcetype='snmp:trap' where `count` grouped by `entity` satisfies detection threshold for 'APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms'. Validate filter `cooling OR compressor OR Compressor OR fan OR Fan OR InRow O`. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-15.1.31 negative (Fault Alarms): ingest benign `power` / `snmp:trap` events where `entity` stays below detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv`. Confirm zero alert rows for 'APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms'.

dataSources: Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) is a container that sends APC InRow and NetShelter traps (enterprise `.1.3.6.1.4.1.318`) to HEC as `sourcetype=sc4snmp:traps` in `netops` unless `splunk.sourcetypeTraps` and `splunk.eventIndex` are overridden. SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) can poll PowerNet-MIB on a heavy forwarder. InRow status is `airIRRCUnitStatus` (`.1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.13.3.2.2.2`); generic cooling uses `coolingUnitStatusDiscreteTable` and `coolingUnitStatusAnalogTable`. There is no `coolingUnitState` object. Key trap fields are `trapoid`, `trap_name`, and `eventName`.
app: Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) container trap receiver (HEC), SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537)
spl:
index=power (sourcetype=snmp:trap OR sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling) host=* trapoid="*318*"
| search cooling OR compressor OR Compressor OR fan OR Fan OR InRow OR Airflow OR airflow OR environmental OR Environmental
| table _time, host, trapoid, trap_name, eventName, _raw
description: Detects UC-15.1.31 — APC, InRow, and, Airflow, Unit — using `index=power` sourcetype `snmp:trap`, grouped by `entity`. Outputs `count` each `the scheduled window`; alert when configured threshold. Filter chain includes filter `cooling OR compressor OR Compressor OR fan OR Fan OR InRow O`.
value: Tracking `activity` via UC-15.1.31 on `snmp:trap` feeds improves response to 'APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms' and reduces operational risk and delayed incident response.
implementation: Stand up the trap path first: deploy Splunk Connect for SNMP (6266) as a container and accept UDP/162 from APC Network Management Card sources. Traps default to `sourcetype=sc4snmp:traps` in `netops`; `index=power` and `sourcetype=snmp:trap` need `splunk.eventIndex` and `splunk.sourcetypeTraps` with parsed `trapoid` and varbind alarm text into a consistent `alarm_text` or CIM-friendly field. For sites that poll instead of trap, define a modular input stanza in the SNMP Modular Input (1537) that walks the APC enterprise cooling OIDs and routes to `sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling`, extracting `airIRRCUnitStatus` (InRow RC) or `coolingUnitStatusDiscreteTable` objects and fan or compressor alarm OIDs documented in your MIB reference. Put a maintenance tag or host lookup in front of alerting so vendor-executed compressor tests during change windows do not page the default queue. Bind the alert action to the data-center facilities roster, attach the thermal escalation SOP, and keep a `-15m` dispatch window aligned to the cron schedule to match the SPL in this UC.
visualization: Dashboard Studio timeline of cooling trap volume on index=power by host; primary table sorted by _time with columns host, trapoid, trap_name, eventName, and parsed alarm_text; single-value KPI for distinct faulting InRow hosts in the last 15 minutes; markdown panel with NMC verification checklist for drilldown; optional Sankey or relationship visualization from trap host to row or aisle using an asset lookup.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `power` (UC-15.1.31)** — Planned work for 'APC InRow and Airflow Unit Compressor or Fan Fault Alarms' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope. Applies filter `cooling OR compressor OR Compressor OR fan OR Fan OR InRow O`. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `snmp:trap`** — Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing configured threshold for UC-15.1.31. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `power` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `snmp:trap`** — First 48h baseline for UC-15.1.31 on `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise 9.2+ or Splunk Cloud search tier with SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) on a heavy forwarder, or Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) deployed as its own container (Docker Compose or microk8s) that forwards traps to HEC. Trap communities and SNMPv3 user secrets live in the SC4SNMP values file.
• RBAC: use the `admin` role on Splunk Enterprise or `sc_admin` on Splunk Cloud to install apps and open `inputs.conf`; grant the operations team a custom role with read access to `index=power` and `edit_monitor` disabled in production.
• Network/firewall: allow SNMP traps (UDP/162) from APC InRow/NMC subnets to the collector; for polling, allow SNMP GET/GET-NEXT (UDP/161) outbound from Splunk to each NMC.

Configure data collection
• Trap path: bind the SC4SNMP listener to the correct interface, set trap communities or SNMPv3 users in the SC4SNMP values file (not a per-device IP list on the forwarder), and verify the first trap shows `sourcetype=sc4snmp:traps` in `netops` unless you override the index and sourcetype, with `trapoid` containing `.1.3.6.1.4.1.318`.
• Enable rich parsing (`full_json`, `VARBINDS`, or equivalent) so `trap_name`, `eventName`, and raw varbind strings are searchable for keywords like compressor, fan, airflow, or InRow.
• Polling path: create an SNMP Modular Input profile with a 60–120s interval, normalize output to `sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling`, and confirm `airIRRCUnitStatus` or `coolingUnitStatusDiscrete*` objects plus fault OIDs populate after a walk of the APC enterprise branch.

Create and tune the correlation
• Start from the packaged SPL baseline: constrain to `host=*`, `trapoid="*318*"`, and (for dual path) `(sourcetype=snmp:trap OR sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling)`.
• Add `streamstats` or `transaction` keyed by host and trap signature inside a `-15m` window to collapse flap duplicates before alerting.
• Optional: `lookup` enrich host -> row ID so dashboards separate aisle containment zones.

Validate
• Replay a sanitized trap `_raw` sample in search using `index=power sourcetype=snmp:trap` over `-24h@h` and compare timestamps with the APC web UI alarm history on the same NMC.
• For polled feeds, chart `_time` vs `airIRRCUnitStatus` or the cooling-unit status object you poll and confirm gaps align with SNMP timeouts rather than silent drops.

Operationalize and troubleshoot
• Route alerts to facilities on-call with throttle keyed on host + trap signature; attach links to rack inlet temperature dashboards.
• If dual-published to a BMS, document precedence (Splunk vs BMS source of truth) to avoid duplicate tickets.
• Common failures: SNMP ACL changes on NMC (symptom: sudden zero events), clock skew (symptom: traps appear outside drill windows), SC4SNMP restart clearing dedup state (symptom: alert storm) — capture in the runbook with restart and ACL checks.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the physical data center for power, cooling, environment, and physical access.
